theater: 伊比利亞半島葡萄牙與西班牙邊境

battle.name: 橘子戰爭
battle.theater: 伊比利亞半島葡萄牙與西班牙邊境
battle.brief: 一八〇一年二月十九日，西班牙以斷絕英葡同盟的最後通牒與奧利文薩邊界爭端向葡萄牙開戰，交火落在伊比利亞半島邊境。葡軍死守埃爾瓦斯與坎普馬約爾堡壘，西軍久攻不下，五月三十日巴達霍斯和約割奧利文薩。英軍分遣隊攜帶的一七五七年式步槍，是英國線列步兵的制式火槍，並逐步裝備葡軍。

kit.name: 一七五七年式步槍
kit.history: 一七五七年式步槍是英國陸軍線列步兵的制式火槍，配置於步兵連與營的射擊單位，屬於步兵部隊的基本地面槍械。

countries: 一八〇一年的橘子戰爭，交戰方是葡萄牙王國與西班牙王國、法蘭西第一共和國三方，葡萄牙一方的葡屬巴西亦有份參與，是第二次反法同盟框架下的戰事。葡萄牙由女王瑪麗亞一世與攝政王若昂主持國政，軍隊骨幹是十餘個線列步兵營與若干炮兵連，另有地方民兵與義勇分隊；作戰重點在阿連特茹的邊境，據點由洛萊、埃爾瓦斯、胡羅梅尼亞與奧利文薩串聯，防守縱深一直伸到里斯本外圍。西班牙由卡洛斯四世統治，實際推動戰爭的是首相兼大元帥戈多伊，他主張以軍事手段迫令里斯本關閉港口、斷絕與英國的同盟；入侵縱隊以埃斯特雷馬杜拉軍團為主，下轄五個師，沿瓜迪阿納河東岸與邊境道路推進。法國在幕後煽動並派兵支援，一八〇一年四月法軍抵達葡萄牙，葡軍要同時應付兩面。法國與西班牙合計的兵力，中文維基條目所列為六萬人，葡軍則為一萬八千人。英國不是條約交戰國，但自一七九三年起便與葡萄牙訂有同盟，戰事一開即派皇家海軍分遣隊巡弋葡西近海，戰後更以克林頓上校率三千五百名英軍佔領馬德拉群島，直到《亞眠和約》簽訂。
countriesEn: The War of the Oranges of 1801 was fought between the Kingdom of Portugal on one side and the Kingdom of Spain together with the French First Republic on the other, and Portuguese Brazil also took a share on the Portuguese side; the war belonged to the framework of the Second Coalition. Portugal was governed by Queen Maria I and the Prince Regent John, with a military whose backbone was a dozen or more line infantry battalions and a number of artillery companies, supplemented by provincial militia and volunteer detachments. Its fighting weight lay along the frontier of the Alentejo, where the positions of Loulé, Elvas, Juromenha and Olivença were linked in a chain whose defensive depth reached the outskirts of Lisbon. Spain was ruled by Charles IV, and the effective driver of the war was the prime minister and captain general Godoy, who wanted military means to force Lisbon to break its alliance with Britain and to close its ports. His invading column was centred on the Estremadura Corps, which was organised into five divisions and pushed forward along the east bank of the Guadiana and the border roads. France stirred the business up behind the scenes and sent troops in support: French troops reached Portugal in April 1801, and the Portuguese army had to face two fronts at once. The Chinese Wikipedia entry gives sixty thousand men for Spain and France together and eighteen thousand for Portugal. Britain was not a party to the treaties, but it had been in alliance with Portugal since 1793, and as soon as the war began it sent a Royal Navy detachment into the waters between the two countries; after the fighting it occupied the island of Madeira with three thousand five hundred men under Colonel Clinton and did not leave until the Treaty of Amiens was signed.
people: 里斯本方面，攝政王若昂（後來的若昂六世）是真正的決策者；女王瑪麗亞一世此時健康惡化，幾乎不問政事，戰事一開便急向倫敦求援。葡軍的統帥是拉豐伊什的若昂公爵，貝雷斯福德以英國將領身分出任他的軍事顧問，替葡軍整編編制、訓練射擊與供應線；前線的堅守多由中校迪亞斯·阿澤維多與將軍弗朗西斯科·德·諾羅尼亞負責，前者在坎普馬約爾抵禦西班牙兩個師的圍攻達十七日，後者在埃爾瓦斯擊退戈多伊親自率領的主力。荷蘭入籍葡萄牙的將領亨里克·德·施米爾姆彭寧率領前線步兵作戰，阿爾布費拉一役的野戰指揮即出於他。西班牙方面，首相戈多伊幾乎親自過問每一步驟，坎普馬約爾的圍城亦由他直接指揮；他的作法最終成為一則插話的由來——他在埃爾瓦斯外摘下橘子送給王后瑪麗亞·路易莎，附言稱即將攻入里斯本。法國方面由洛朗·德·古維翁·聖西爾率軍入葡支援。英國方面，首相小威廉·皮特與陸軍大臣亨利·鄧達斯把援助葡萄牙視為阻止法國取得伊比利亞半島港口的一環；據載一八〇一年春有由理查德·比克頓率領的分遣隊在奧埃拉斯一帶登陸，與葡方保持軍事聯絡，戰後則有克林頓上校率三千五百名英軍進駐馬德拉。關於雙方傷亡人數，各家記載互相矛盾、無從核對，本實錄因此不列任何看似精確的傷亡數字。
peopleEn: In Lisbon the real decision maker was the Prince Regent John, later John VI of Portugal; Queen Maria I was in poor health and took almost no part in government, and the moment war broke out the court appealed to London. The Portuguese army was commanded by the Duke of Lafões, with Beresford acting as his military adviser in the capacity of a British officer and reorganising the establishment, the drill and the supply system of the Portuguese troops. The defence of the frontier positions was in the hands of Colonel Dias Azevedo and General Francisco de Noronha: the former held Campo Maior for seventeen days against two Spanish divisions, the latter beat back the main force led by Godoy in person at Elvas. The Dutch-born officer in Portuguese service Henrique de Schimmelpennig led the infantry in the field, and it was he who held the field command at Albufeira. On the Spanish side the prime minister Godoy followed almost every step in person and directed the siege of Campo Maior himself; the manner of his conduct later supplied the story behind the nickname, for he picked oranges outside the fortress of Elvas and sent them to the queen Maria Luisa with the message that he would soon be entering Lisbon. On the French side the army that came to support the Spanish was led by Laurent de Gouvion Saint-Cyr. On the British side the prime minister the younger William Pitt and the secretary of state for war Henry Dundas treated the support of Portugal as a means of denying France her Iberian ports; by one account a detachment under Richard Bickerton landed in the neighbourhood of Oeiras in the spring of 1801 and kept up the military link with the Portuguese, and after the war Colonel Clinton took three thousand five hundred British soldiers to Madeira. Casualty figures for the two sides are mutually contradictory and cannot be checked against one another, so no figure that looks precise is given here.
kits: 本卡兵器一七五七年式步槍，是英國陸軍自一七五七年起列裝的制式滑膛燧發步槍，也是十八世紀末至十九世紀初英軍線列步兵的基本地面槍械。槍身為長約四十二吋的一點零六公尺單身管，口徑約零點五七英吋，配燧發機件，燧石由可翻起的護板壓住而點燃底火；槍口原留插銷式刺刀的位置，後改裝矛式刺刀，一七八二年式的矛式刺刀是當時英軍的標準配備。發射用火藥、鉛彈與火帽分裝，每兵標準備彈六十發，射速約每分鐘三至四發，有效射程約二百公尺，超出此距彈道便急遽失準。在橘子戰爭中，這件兵器由英國分遣隊攜帶，並以英國軍械庫的存量逐步補充葡萄牙線列步兵；葡軍各營裝備並不一致，部分營仍沿用十八世紀中葉的舊式火槍，守備奧利文薩與胡羅梅尼亞的甚至只是民兵。西班牙線列步兵使用西班牙自製的十八世紀燧發滑膛步槍，口徑約零點五八英吋，同樣以刺刀作近戰兵器，並未普遍改用雷管槍。炮兵方面，英葡分隊配六磅滑膛野戰炮，西班牙縱隊另有八磅與十二磅炮，圍攻坎普馬約爾達十七日者已動用攻城炮與圍城器材；邊境要塞如胡羅梅尼亞與埃爾瓦斯一帶的堡壘則架設青銅炮與舊式鐵炮，法軍入葡時亦攜帶法式野戰炮。運輸依靠牛車與騾隊，彈藥分載於營部彈藥箱、炮架箱與彈藥車，各營每日耗彈量無從核實。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card, the Pattern 1757 Musket, was the standard smoothbore flintlock musket adopted by the British army from 1757 and the basic infantry arm of the line battalions from the late eighteenth into the early nineteenth century. It had a single barrel about forty-two inches long, that is roughly 1.06 metres, of about 0.577 inch calibre, worked by a flintlock in which the flint was held by a pivoted frizzen that struck the pan; the muzzle had originally been drilled to take a plug bayonet and was later fitted for the socket bayonet, the socket bayonet of 1782 being the standard of the British army at the time. It fired loose ammunition of powder, ball and priming, with sixty rounds per man as the standard issue, a rate of fire of about three to four rounds a minute and an effective range of some two hundred metres, beyond which the fall of shot was rapidly lost. In the War of the Oranges this arm was carried by the British detachment and was passed on to the Portuguese line infantry from the stores of the British ordnance; the equipment of the Portuguese battalions was not uniform, and some still used older eighteenth century muskets, while the garrisons of Olivença and Juromenha were no more than militia. The Spanish line infantry used Spanish-made eighteenth century flintlock muskets of about 0.58 inch calibre, likewise with the bayonet for close work, and had not yet gone over to percussion generally. In the artillery arm, the British and Portuguese detachments had six-pounder smoothbore field guns, the Spanish column had eight and twelve pounders as well, and the seventeen-day siege of Campo Maior had already brought up siege guns and the equipment of a blockade; the frontier works at Juromenha and around Elvas mounted bronze and older iron guns, and the French who entered Portugal brought French field pieces with them. Transport was by ox cart and mule, ammunition was carried in regimental ammunition boxes, on limber boxes and in ammunition wagons, and no daily rate of consumption can be verified for any battalion.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術主軸是攻守要塞，而不是野戰決勝負。西班牙入侵縱隊渡過瓜迪阿納河之後分兵指向幾個明確目標：主力壓向埃爾瓦斯堡壘，兩個師指向坎普馬約爾，一個師指向奧利文薩與胡羅梅尼亞。後兩處的工事尚未完工，守軍只有數百人而且多為民兵，很快便向西班牙軍投降；坎普馬約爾的葡軍卻在中校迪亞斯·阿澤維多指揮下據城死守十七日，迫使西班牙軍投入兩個完整的師與攻城炮列。戈多伊親自率領的主力攻打埃爾瓦斯要塞，卻被弗朗西斯科·德·諾羅尼亞率領的葡軍守軍擊退，砲火未能撼動棱堡射界。西班牙軍此後退到遠離要塞的安全距離，戈多伊直到戰爭結束都不再進攻，大批西班牙兵力被釘在圍城戰中，其餘各部也無法突破葡軍主力對內陸道路的封鎖，戰局遂成僵局。另一份常見的戰史則記錄二月末至三月間坎普馬約爾與阿爾布費拉兩場會戰：西班牙軍在阿爾布費拉擊敗葡軍，卻仍無力攻破要塞，也未能打通到里斯本的道路。葡軍整體採取守勢與遲滯抵抗，把民兵與地方武裝編入沿線據點，構成多層次的抵抗，並把英軍分遣隊與精銳骨幹營留在里斯本附近作為預備隊，寧可讓邊線受壓也不投入正面會戰。現有史料足以確認上述戰術階段，卻不足以為每個步兵營指定射擊路線與個別射界。
tacticsEn: The tactical centre of this war was the assault on and the defence of fortresses, not a decision in the open field. After crossing the Guadiana the Spanish invading column divided towards several definite objectives: the main body pressed against the fortress of Elvas, two divisions moved on Campo Maior and one division moved on Olivença and Juromenha. At the last two the works were not yet finished and the garrisons numbered only a few hundred men, mostly militia, so both fell quickly to the Spanish; the Portuguese at Campo Maior, however, held the town for seventeen days under Colonel Dias Azevedo, and forced the Spanish to commit two full divisions and a siege train to the business. The main body led by Godoy in person attacked the fortress of Elvas and was repulsed by the Portuguese garrison under Francisco de Noronha, the artillery failing to shift the fire of the bastions. The Spanish then withdrew to a safe distance from the fortresses and Godoy did not attack again before the war ended: the bulk of the Spanish army was pinned down in the siege operations, while the rest could not break through the blockade of the inland roads maintained by the main Portuguese force, and the situation became a stalemate. Another account, the one more commonly given, records two battles at the end of February and in March, at Campo Maior and at Albufeira: the Spanish army beat the Portuguese at Albufeira, yet it still could not take the fortresses and could not open the road to Lisbon. On the Portuguese side the plan as a whole was one of defence and delaying action, with the militia and local armed bands woven into the line of posts to make a defence in several layers, while the British detachment and the best of the line battalions were kept near Lisbon as a reserve, the border being allowed to be pressed rather than risking a general action. The surviving material is enough to confirm those stages of the fighting, but not enough to assign a firing line or a specific field of fire to each infantry battalion.
data: 可寫而有根據的數字，以中文維基條目所列者最為齊整：交戰方一欄明列法國與西班牙對葡萄牙，葡屬巴西亦列於葡方。時間線上，西班牙於一八〇一年二月十九日宣布開戰，葡萄牙於二月二十日宣戰；一八〇一年四月法軍抵達葡萄牙，西班牙軍亦同時加入；五月二十日前後西班牙軍自邊境向埃爾瓦斯、坎普馬約爾、奧利文薩與胡羅梅尼亞展開攻勢，坎普馬約爾的圍城歷時十七日。五月二十五日奧利文薩要塞守軍投降，五月三十日在巴達霍斯簽訂和約，葡方於六月六日正式接受條款，九月廿九日再追加接受《馬德里條約》的修改；該條目把交戰期間記為五月廿日至六月九日，與二月宣戰的說法並不一致，本實錄兩說並存。兵力方面，中文維基條目所列葡軍為一萬八千人，西班牙與法國合計六萬人；守備奧利文薩與胡羅梅尼亞者只有數百人，多為民兵。英軍方面，一八〇一年春在奧埃拉斯登陸的分遣隊一般記為約七百五十人；一八〇一年七月至《亞眠和約》前，克林頓上校率三千五百名英軍佔領馬德拉群島。距離上，里斯本至埃爾瓦斯約二百二十公里，埃爾瓦斯至奧利文薩約二十公里，阿爾布費拉距里斯本約一百四十公里，瓜迪阿納河是縱隊越境的主要門戶。傷亡方面沒有可信的統一統計，可確定的只是坎普馬約爾與阿爾布費拉兩役均有數百人傷亡與被俘，具體數目各方說法互相矛盾，本實錄不予填補。就火力節奏而言，一七五七年式步槍每兵備彈六十發、射速每分鐘三至四發，是當時線列步兵的射擊基準。
dataEn: The numbers that can be written down with some foundation are most complete in the Chinese Wikipedia entry, whose list of belligerents names France and Spain against Portugal, with Portuguese Brazil on the Portuguese side. As to the sequence of events, Spain declared war on the nineteenth of February 1801 and Portugal answered on the twentieth; in April 1801 French troops reached Portugal and the Spanish army came in with them; around the twentieth of May the Spanish army moved from the frontier towards Elvas, Campo Maior, Olivença and Juromenha, and the siege of Campo Maior lasted seventeen days. The garrison of the fortress of Olivença surrendered on the twenty-fifth of May, the peace was signed at Badajoz on the thirtieth, Portugal formally accepted the terms on the sixth of June and on the twenty-ninth of September additionally accepted the modifications made to the Treaty of Madrid; the same entry gives the period of fighting as the twentieth of May to the ninth of June, which does not agree with the declaration of war in February, and both accounts are therefore given here. As to strength, the Chinese entry gives eighteen thousand Portuguese against sixty thousand Spaniards and French together, while the garrisons of Olivença and Juromenha numbered only a few hundred, mostly militia. On the British side the detachment that landed at Oeiras in the spring of 1801 is generally given as about seven hundred and fifty men, and from July 1801 until the Treaty of Amiens Colonel Clinton held the island of Madeira with three thousand five hundred British soldiers. As to distances, Lisbon is about two hundred and twenty kilometres from Elvas by road, Elvas is about twenty kilometres from Olivença, Albufeira lies about a hundred and forty kilometres from Lisbon, and the Guadiana was the gateway by which the column crossed into Portugal. There is no reliable overall casualty return: what can be said is that the actions at Campo Maior and Albufeira each cost several hundred men killed, wounded and taken prisoner, the exact figures being mutually contradictory, so none is supplied here. As for the rhythm of fire, the Pattern 1757 musket with sixty rounds per man and a rate of three to four shots a minute sets the firing standard of the line infantry of the time.
cause: 橘子戰爭的起因是三件事疊在一起。第一件是法國與西班牙的施壓：法國第一執政拿破崙與西班牙首相兼大元帥戈多伊於一八〇〇年向葡萄牙發出最後通牒，要求她斷絕與英國的同盟、關閉港口，葡萄牙拒絕讓步，衝突遂由貿易與外交轉為兵戎。第二件是法國直接出兵：一八〇一年四月法軍抵達葡萄牙，戈多伊指揮的西班牙軍隨即加入，使葡軍要同時應付兩面進攻。第三件是邊界與要塞的實際爭奪：奧利文薩及周邊地區的歸屬在《馬德里條約》劃界後長期不一致，兩國軍方曾數次進入對方視為己有的據點，攻守要塞成為爭議的最終解決方式。至於「橘子」這個名稱，至少有兩種說法並存：一說葡國士兵在邊界衝突中把從俘虜那裡取來的橘子擲回西班牙士兵；另一說是戈多伊在埃爾瓦斯要塞外摘下橘子送給王后瑪麗亞·路易莎，並附言稱即將攻入里斯本，後世以此為戰爭命名。兩說都只解釋稱號，邊界、通牒與同盟才是開戰的真正理由。
causeEn: Three things came together to bring about the War of the Oranges. The first was the pressure of France and Spain: in 1800 the First Consul of France Napoleon and the prime minister and captain general of Spain Godoy put a last warning to Portugal, requiring her to break her alliance with Britain and to close her ports; Portugal refused to give way, and the quarrel turned from trade and diplomacy into fighting. The second was the direct entry of French troops: in April 1801 the French army reached Portugal and the Spanish army under Godoy joined it, so that the Portuguese had to face attacks on two fronts. The third was the actual contest over frontier fortresses: the ownership of Olivença and of the districts around it remained inconsistent after the demarcation in the Treaty of Madrid, the troops of both countries had more than once entered places the other regarded as its own, and the assault on the fortresses became the final form the dispute took. As for the name, at least two stories are current and both are given: one says that Portuguese soldiers took oranges from the saddlebags of prisoners and threw them back at Spanish soldiers during a border clash; the other says that Godoy picked oranges outside the fortress of Elvas and sent them to the queen Maria Luisa with the message that he would soon be entering Lisbon, and the war was named from that. Both stories explain the title only; the frontier, the ultimatum and the alliance are the real reasons for the war.
impact: 對葡萄牙而言，這場戰爭的直接結果是保住國土，間接結果是把國家更深地綁在英國身上。葡軍守住了埃爾瓦斯與坎普馬約爾，沒有崩潰；貝雷斯福德整編的線列步兵、炮兵與後勤體系自此成為英國在半島上倚重的支撐，葡國的港口與兵源開始定期供應英軍，而英國的撥款、軍官與軍械也持續流入葡軍，這種互賴在後來的半島戰爭中成為英國陸軍在伊比利亞立足的基礎。戰後英國更以克林頓上校率三千五百名英軍進駐馬德拉群島，直至《亞眠和約》簽訂才撤出，其間葡萄牙默許此事，等於用葡國的領土換取海上的保護。對西班牙而言，這是一場得不償失的勝利：埃爾瓦斯攻不下，阿爾布費拉得勝也未能打通通往里斯本的道路，戈多伊的封鎖要求完全落空，戰爭卻留下一個「橘子」的笑柄，馬德里的宮廷與輿論都飽受嘲弄，法國甚至撕毀《巴達霍斯條約》。更長遠的影響落在奧利文薩：葡萄牙割讓該地之後，一八一一年葡軍曾重新佔領，一八一五年前後的維也納會議要求戰勝國盡最大努力使奧利文薩歸還葡萄牙，但西班牙並未執行，葡萄牙在一八六一年的戰爭中再度拿下並保留至今，兩國對該地的爭議至今未決。從大格局看，這場戰爭是拿破崙時代英國在伊比利亞半島爭奪港口與資源的一環，它把葡萄牙推上反法同盟的前線，也加深了葡西兩國的世仇，並在一八〇七年法軍入侵、葡王室遷往巴西之後被重新翻出來算帳。
impactEn: For Portugal the direct result of the war was the preservation of the country, and the indirect result was a tighter binding of the nation to Britain. The Portuguese army held at Elvas and at Campo Maior and did not break; the line infantry, artillery and supply system reformed by Beresford became a support on which Britain relied in the peninsula, Portuguese ports and manpower began to feed the British army on a regular basis, and British money, officers and stores continued to flow into the Portuguese army, and that reciprocity in the later Peninsular War became the foundation on which the British army stood in Iberia. After the war the British went further and kept three thousand five hundred men on Madeira under Colonel Clinton until the Treaty of Amiens, with the connivance of Portugal, so that Portuguese territory was exchanged for protection at sea. For Spain it was a victory that cost more than it gained: Elvas could not be taken, the win at Albufeira opened no road to Lisbon, Godoy's demands for a blockade came to nothing, and the war left behind the laughing stock of the oranges, mocked in the Madrid court and in public opinion, while France tore up the Treaty of Badajoz altogether. The longer effect fell on Olivença: after Portugal had ceded the town, Portuguese troops occupied it again in 1811, and the Congress of Vienna of 1815 called on the victorious powers to make every effort to restore Olivença to Portugal, which Spain did not carry out; Portugal took the town once more in the war of 1861 and has kept it ever since, and the dispute between the two countries over it is still unsettled. Seen in the wider frame, this war was one of the English struggles for Iberian ports and resources in the age of Napoleon; it pushed Portugal to the front of the anti-French coalition, it deepened the enmity between the two Iberian kingdoms, and it was dug up again and called to account after the French invasion of 1807 and the flight of the Portuguese court to Brazil.
result: 一八〇一年五月三十日，葡萄牙與西班牙在巴達霍斯簽訂和約，葡方於六月六日正式接受條款。按條約，葡萄牙關閉港口、禁止英國船隻停靠，給予法國商業特權，並把奧利文薩割讓給西班牙、支付賠款；西班牙則歸還其餘所佔的葡萄牙領土。就戰場而言，葡萄牙守住了埃爾瓦斯與坎普馬約爾的堡壘，西班牙大軍攻不下便退到安全距離，戰爭以僵局收場，雙方都沒有得到決定性的地面勝利，戈多伊直到戰事結束都不敢再攻。奧利文薩一地成為雙方談判的焦點，割讓與賠款換來和平，卻把爭議留到後世：葡軍於一八〇五年特拉法加海戰失利後與英國恢復關係，法國隨即宣廢《巴達霍斯條約》並於一八〇七年再侵葡萄牙，葡王室遷往巴西；若昂六世後來在里約熱內盧譴責該條約乃在脅迫下簽訂、宣布無效。戰後各方的評論眾說紛紜：西班牙把失敗歸咎於圍城與補給，葡軍內部則為坎普馬約爾與阿爾布費拉的損失，以及貝雷斯福德與拉豐伊什公爵之間的責任歸屬爭論不休，這些指責至今仍留在戰史記載之中。
resultEn: On the thirtieth of May 1801 Portugal and Spain signed the peace at Badajoz, and Portugal formally accepted the terms on the sixth of June. Under the treaty Portugal closed its ports and barred British ships from sheltering in them, granted commercial privileges to France, and ceded Olivença to Spain together with an indemnity; Spain in return restored the rest of the Portuguese territory it had occupied. On the field the Portuguese held the fortresses of Elvas and Campo Maior, the Spanish army could not take them and withdrew to a safe distance, and the war ended in a stalemate with no decisive ground victory for either side; Godoy did not dare to attack again before the fighting was over. Olivença became the focus of the negotiations, and the cession and the indemnity bought peace at the price of leaving the dispute for posterity: after the Portuguese navy was beaten at Trafalgar in 1805 and Portugal restored relations with Britain, France declared the Treaty of Badajoz void and invaded Portugal again in 1807, and the Portuguese court moved to Brazil; in Rio de Janeiro John VI later denounced the treaty as signed under duress and declared it null. The comments of the time are divided: Spain blamed the sieges and the supply system, while inside the Portuguese army the losses at Campo Maior and Albufeira, and the question of responsibility as between Beresford and the Duke of Lafões, were argued over at length, and those accusations remain in the histories.
